newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Aer Rianta ponders float of international units.
newsitem.headline: Aer Rianta ponders float of international units.

text.p: The head of Ireland's state-owned Aer Rianta airport authority said in remarks published on Friday the company is considering floating its international operations to raise cash for overseas expansion.
Chief Executive Derek Keogh told the Irish Times that a team of consultants would be appointed shortly to consider options for Aer Rianta International (ARI).
He said one option could be to bring in a strategic partner, pension fund or flotation to "find the best way forward in terms of securing finance."
Keogh said the process would be completed by the year's end.
Aer Rianta manages Ireland's three main airports at Dublin, Shannon and Cork. It is part-owner of Birmingham international airport and is part of a consortium bidding for Duesseldorf airport.

ARI has management contracts to run duty free and retailing facilities at both ends of Eurotunnel, Brusnichoye on the Russian/Finnish border, Moscow,Kiev, St Petersburg, Kuwait, Bahrain, Damascus, Karachi, Beijing and Hong Kong.
Keogh said several European airports are currently being privatised, including Naples and Rome, Stuttgart and Hamburg and in Portugal.
He said the company would bid for stakes in European airports which come on the market as well as targeting Asia and the Pacific Rim.
Keogh said he was disappointed to lose the contract to manage Bangkok's downtown duty-free shop at its World Trade Centre but was optimistic about other options.
Management contracts generated revenue but ownership of airports was more lucrative, he said.
"Airports are a long-term business but a good solid business which give a strong return on investment," he told the newspaper.
Ownership of airports was also "much less risky than duty-free" he said, especially in light of EU moves to abolish duty-free shopping in two years' time.

Last year Aer Rianta group reported pre-tax profits of 42.4 million Irish pounds, a 13 percent rise on the previous year. ARI had international sales of 251 million pounds, even higher than the parent group.
